findings.claim: Scope and sequencing contradict the catalog. lab.json covers (lines 9-11) and objectives (lines 22-30) take in the three S33 topics: create-edit-and-delete-against-the-api, handling-submission-errors-in-forms and ui-tests-with-testing-library-querying-by-role-and-label. Those tasks are 4, 5, 6 and 8. But the cleanup note (line 84) places the lab in 'the module's S32 guided lab slot'. authoring/catalog/react/forms-context-and-crud/module.json sourceCoverageNotes say the module lab is for the S32 Lab-day block 'covering the three S32 topics'; S33 is the next day and is a Project day whose rows are course-project parts P3-P5. Each of those three topic.json files records lab 'course:react', with the reason 'No topic lab. Course project: applied in part P3' (P4 for submission errors, P5 for UI tests) '...(Standard S33 Build block...)'. Commit 402c4853 changed only moduleLabs and track notes in module.json; it did not touch those topic.json files. Result: Standard learners in the S32 slot get JSON CRUD, server-error handling and writing a Testing Library test one day before those topic pages are taught, and the catalog says the same objectives belong to the course project.
findings.recommendation: Cut the module lab to the S32 topics (controlled-forms, accessible-forms, sharing-state-with-context). That means tasks 1-3 and 7, plus a given or stubbed onSave, and leaves the CRUD, submission-error and UI-test work to course project parts P3-P5 as the catalog plans. If the captain wants the wider scope instead, first move the slot and update module.json and the three topic.json lab fields so the lab follows the S33 teaching, then re-time it.

findings.claim: The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap (lines 86-89) are not plausible for this task set. This is reasoned from the starter, not measured. The learner must: fix three controlled controls; convert a span to a label and add ids, htmlFor and required; write handleSubmit with preventDefault, two-field validation, fieldErrors state, conditional error paragraphs and aria-describedby/aria-invalid; track a pending state; write try/catch/finally that splits 400 field errors from network failures, plus a role=alert banner; write sendJson with 204 handling and error.status/error.details from a possibly unparsable body; write createService, updateService and deleteService; write handleDelete with toast and refetch; build a full context provider and hook; and write a five-step Testing Library test. That is 8 tasks across 5 files, most of them component work. The accepted comparable lab, html-css-js/fetch-and-browser-client, budgets 38 minutes median and 45 cap for seven single-function tasks in one file.
findings.recommendation: Prefer reducing scope (see edu-fcc-1) so that four or so focused tasks fit 25/30. If the scope stays, re-estimate from a dry run and state the figure honestly in lab.json and the README.

findings.claim: Task 8 is scored only by whether the learner's own test passes. lab.json notes (line 84) honestly call the ui-tests objectives 'honor-verified', but the learner-facing README (lines 47-49, 99-101) never says so. This was observed in a scratch copy: deleting only the placeholder 'expect(true).toBe(false)' (starter/src/service-form.test.jsx line 38) and running that file against the UNMODIFIED starter ServiceForm, which shows no errors at all, gives '1 passed (1)'. So an empty test turns task 8 green regardless of the form. Nothing checks that the test queries by role or label, uses user-event, or would catch a broken form. So ui-tests#o1-o3 are listed in lab.json objectives (lines 28-30) while being practised but not scored. The accepted fetch-and-browser-client lab instead runs the learner's test against deliberately broken copies.
findings.recommendation: Add a mutation check: run the learner's test file against a ServiceForm variant that never shows 'Enter a service name.', or that calls onSave on blank input, and require it to fail. Otherwise, at minimum, tell learners in the README that test 8 only proves their test passes and is self-checked, and keep the honor-verified note.

findings.claim: Step 5 (lines 14-16) contradicts itself on the exact skill ui-tests#o2 teaches (choosing getBy, queryBy or findBy). It says to 'assert with findBy that the error disappears' and then adds '(queryBy is the variant that proves an element is absent)'. findBy waits for an element to appear and rejects when it is absent, so it cannot assert disappearance. A learner who follows the instruction literally writes a test that fails on a correct form. Step 5 also says to 'type a name and a team with user-event', but the team control is a <select>, which needs user.selectOptions, not type.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 along these lines: 'then type a name with user.type, choose a team with user.selectOptions, submit again, and assert with queryBy that the error is gone (wrap it in waitFor if it disappears asynchronously) and that onSave was called with the values.'

findings.claim: The README does not disclose cross-task test coupling. On the shipped starter, tests 4-7 all fail with task 2's message ('Found a label with the text of: Service name, however no form control was found associated to that label'), not with anything about their own task; this was observed by running npm test on a copy of the snapshot. Test 7 also needs the 'Service deleted' toast, which is written in TASK 6 (OverviewPage.jsx lines 27-37). Yet the README's task 6 summary (lines 94-96) never mentions the toast, test 6 does not assert it, and the 'Files you edit' list maps task 7 only to ToastContext.jsx. A learner whose test 7 fails on 'Service deleted' is pointed at the wrong file.
findings.recommendation: Under 'How to test', add one or two sentences, as the auth-and-review README does for its coupling: tests 4-7 build on tasks 1-3, and test 7 also checks the delete toast you add in task 6. Add 'announce "Service deleted"' to the README task 6 summary.

findings.claim: The troubleshooting entry 'Task 4's test hangs - make sure handleSubmit awaits onSave inside try/finally so the button re-enables even on failure' describes a symptom that does not occur. This is reasoned from tests/t4-create-service.test.jsx and tests/t5-server-errors.test.jsx. Test 4 cannot hang: its waitFor and findBy calls time out in about 1 s and the test fails normally. A button that never re-enables after a failure surfaces in test 5 instead: after the first 400, the second 'Save service' click lands on a disabled button and nothing submits, so findByRole('alert') reports 'Unable to find role="alert"'.
findings.recommendation: Reword the entry: 'Test 5 cannot find the alert after the first error - the Save button probably stayed disabled; reset the pending state in finally so it re-enables after a failure.'

findings.recommendation: Say it explicitly: 'the team caption is a <span>; make it a <label> and point it at the select with htmlFor'.

findings.claim: controlled-forms#o2 ('Handle form submission with onSubmit and event.preventDefault') is claimed, but no test scores the preventDefault clause. Reasoned from the starter run: in jsdom, the submit event still reaches React's onSubmit whether or not the default is prevented. Omitting preventDefault only prints the unexplained stderr trace 'Error: Not implemented: HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit', which appears on the shipped-starter run under test 3, and the README troubleshooting never explains it.
findings.recommendation: Either assert that the submit event was default-prevented, for example with a capture-phase submit listener in test 3 that checks event.defaultPrevented, or record a partial-objective note for o2. Add a troubleshooting line mapping the jsdom 'requestSubmit' message to a missing event.preventDefault().

findings.claim: The setup commands do not work when run in order. The first block runs 'cd tests' (line 27), and the optional block then runs 'cd starter' (line 34), which fails from inside tests/. The next section then says 'From the tests folder', while the learner who followed the optional block is now in starter/.
findings.recommendation: Use 'cd ../starter' in the optional block, or prefix both blocks with 'From the coding-lab folder'. Also say that the dev server keeps that terminal busy, so tests run in a second terminal from tests/.
